name: pattern-list
title: A list from a template and a data list
summary: A favourites list whose five rows are one ContactRow template (definePattern) inflated by patternForEach over a list of names; each row derives its avatar initial from its name with textSubtext, and the name list is hoisted out of the layout with a global section.
prompt: A favourites contact list (Ada Lovelace, Barbara Liskov, Claude Shannon, Edsger Dijkstra, Grace Hopper): each row has a round avatar with the initial, the name and a chevron, built from one row definition repeated over the list of names.
teaches: Define a row once with definePattern (parameter who) and repeat it for every item of a data list with patternForEach {collection, localItem, children}
Pass the current item to the template by name: {"ContactRow": {"who": "@name"}}, where name is the patternForEach localItem
Derive per-row values inside the template from its parameter (textSubtext of @who gives the avatar initial), so the data list stays one string per row
Hoist the data list out of the layout with a global section in a canvas: it is written before the root, like a resource
pitfalls: addDataList cannot be named in the Java parser (U4), so collection is the list's numeric id: 2097194 (0x20002A) for the first array of a document. A floatArrays resource or another list before it moves that id
addDataList is a canvas command, not a component: it needs a canvas around it (here a 0-size one, its command wrapped in global)
A pattern name must not match a built-in component case-insensitively: a template called Row fails with "Cannot override pre-existing component"
patternForEach gives one id per item; a row needing several fields needs them derived from that one string (or one template call per row instead of a data list)

snippets.note: patternForEach over list 2097194, item bound to name, one ContactRow call per item
the names list, hoisted before the root

check.describe: Five rows under FAVOURITES, in list order, each with a blue initial avatar (A, B, C, E, G), the full name and a grey chevron. Resized (narrow 220, wide 540) every inflated row fills the width with the chevron at the right edge; a long name ellipsizes on one line.
